palette.notes: Palette, outlines and lighting are not discussed; the article is purely about motion of 48x92 px fighter sprites.

silhouette: Stance defines the character: a boxer with hands up, neck tucked and soft knees versus a low, wide karate stance; loose clothing and hair thicken and change the outline.

motion.timing: 8-frame idle loop: frames 1-4 at 100 ms, frames 5-8 at 50 ms, so the rise and apex linger and the drop is fast. Body moves 1 px per step; fists and arms 2-4 px.
principles: weight via knee and heel shifts

texture: Fabric wrinkles and loose areas shift slightly each frame; added only after the base body loop works.

acting.acts: The idle is the personality display: torso anchors the bounce, limbs lag or lead by different pixel amounts, head stays level on the last frame while legs extend.
acting.depth: One sprite at one scale; offsets are counted in single pixels, so it only works at native resolution.

techniques: split timing: 4 frames at 100 ms up, 4 frames at 50 ms down = gravity
different body parts move different distances (body 1 px, fists 2-4 px)
heels lift for the top of the bounce, knees compress for the bottom
torso as the anchor; limbs and hair overlap it
base form-fitting loop first, then add secondary motion one area at a time
head stays level while legs extend to avoid a bobbing head
feel: 8-frame breath + slow top, fast drop + 1 px body vs 3 px fists = an idle with weight and attitude
for_fred: Replace Fred's constant looping with one weighted idle: slow rise for 4 frames at 100 ms, fast sink for 4 at 50 ms, body moving 1 px while fins move 2-3 px. Use it only while he waits in frame, so actions read against a calm baseline instead of everything animating at once.
